provenanceNote: No existing test in this repo calls sanitizeTsvField, sanitizeMarkdownField, or sanitizePipelineUrl directly (grepped tests/ and web/ — zero hits as of this commit). These cases were AUTHORED against the live implementation in scan.mjs: each expected value was produced by running the real function, not derived from a pre-existing, independently-verified assertion. That means this fixture file proves a second implementation AGREES with the current JS behaviour — it does NOT prove that behaviour is correct. If the JS itself has a latent bug in one of these functions, this fixture will faithfully freeze that bug into the conformance kit. See the order-dependence and internal-space-truncation notes on individual cases below for behaviour worth a second look before trusting it as intentional.

sanitizeTsvField.note: null coalesces to empty string via `value ?? ''`; JS `undefined` takes the identical nullish path and is not encoded separately
CSV-injection char = alone, must be neutralized with a leading quote
a leading char outside the =+-@ set must NOT be quoted
an injection char that is not the first character must NOT be quoted
leading whitespace is trimmed BEFORE the injection test, so this still gets quoted
embedded newline collapses to a single space
embedded tab collapses to a single space (protects TSV column alignment)
multiple \r\n in a row collapse to exactly one space
runs of 2+ literal spaces collapse to one
TSV sanitizer does NOT escape pipe (contrast with sanitizeMarkdownField)
TSV sanitizer does NOT escape backslash/brackets at all (contrast with sanitizeMarkdownField/sanitizePipelineUrl)

sanitizeMarkdownField.note: null coalesces to empty string; undefined takes the identical nullish path
a lone backslash is escaped to two backslashes
ORDER-DEPENDENCE case: backslash immediately followed by [ -- catches a Kotlin port doing sequential .replace() calls in the wrong order
ORDER-DEPENDENCE case, reversed: ] immediately followed by backslash
ORDER-DEPENDENCE case, realistic data shape: a Windows path containing a bracketed note
all three escaped characters present together
a single pipe is replaced with / (markdown table column separator)
pipe replaced AND bracket escaped in the same value
sanitizeMarkdownField has NO CSV-injection guard (contrast with sanitizeTsvField) -- a leading = is left alone
embedded newline collapses to a single space
embedded tab collapses to a single space
unicode text (including Turkish) passes through unchanged

sanitizePipelineUrl.note: null coalesces to empty string; undefined takes the identical nullish path
an ordinary URL passes through unchanged
unlike the other two sanitizers, a URL is FIRST-WHITESPACE-TOKEN only -- anything after a space is silently dropped, not collapsed
an embedded newline truncates the same way a space does (both match \s in the split)
an embedded tab truncates the same way
ORDER-DEPENDENCE case on a URL-shaped value: backslash immediately followed by [
all three escaped characters together in one URL
a pipe is replaced with %7C (URL-encoded), NOT / like sanitizeMarkdownField -- because this value rides in a markdown table cell that is ALSO a literal URL
sanitizePipelineUrl has no CSV-injection guard either -- a leading = is left alone
a unicode (IDN/path) URL with no whitespace/bracket/backslash/pipe passes through unchanged
